description: Turns a Royal Mail QR code (the kind you show at a Post Office: Vinted digital labels, eBay Royal Mail QR codes, ASOS returns and other Royal Mail "Labels to Go" QR codes) into a 6x4 shipping label the user can print at home instead of queuing. If the user has an image or PDF of the QR code, call this with no arguments: a panel lets them pick the file, which is read on their device. Only pass qr_text if you already have the exact decoded text from a QR decoder. Never transcribe a QR code from an image.

qr_text.description: The exact text a QR decoder returned for the QR code, unchanged, including every space. It is fields like QRCode=..., 1DBarcode=... and SendersDetails=... separated by |. Omit this if you only have an image of the QR code.

name: create_royal_mail_label

postBy.description: The date to post the parcel by, dd/mm/yyyy.

postcode.description: Last line of the delivery address, normally the postcode.

printUrl.description: Opens the label on Prince of Post, ready to print at its true 6x4 size.

recipient.description: First line of the delivery address.

siteUrl.description: Prince of Post, where the user can drop their QR code if the panel does not appear.

status.description: ready: the label was made from qr_text. needs_file: the user still has to pick their QR code in the panel.

title: Print a Royal Mail QR code as a label
